claim: For \(X_n=(S^0)^{\circledast(n+1)}\), the unique \(2n+2\)-point minimal finite model of \(S^n\) for \(n\ge 1\), every continuous map \(f:X_n\to X_m\) induces a null-homotopic map \(|K(f)|:S^n\to S^m\) unless \(n=m\) and \(f\) is a homeomorphism. Hence minimal sphere models directly realize only the zero class when \(n\ne m\), and exactly the degree classes \(-1,0,1\) when \(n=m\); in particular no nonzero unstable class with \(n>m\), and no self-map of degree \(|d|\ge 2\), is represented without enlarging or subdividing the finite model.

correctness.rationale: The level-rank argument proves that noncollapsed source levels inject strictly into target ranks. Thus n>m forces a collapsed source level; its induced simplicial image is a cone, so the map is null-homotopic. For n=m, absence of a collapse forces every level to map bijectively to the corresponding level, hence a homeomorphism; a collapse again gives nullity. For n<m, pi_n(S^m)=0. Identity and a single-level swap realize degrees +1 and -1.

evidence: Mosquera-Lois arXiv:2608.06176, Theorem 5.3 and Corollary 5.5, force weak homotopy equivalences into facet-essential minimal models to be homeomorphisms.

Hardie–Salbany–Vermeulen–Witbooi's quaternion-multiplication abstract explicitly uses the barycentric subdivision of the minimal S3 model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2026 Whitehead theorem overlaps the equal-dimensional weak-equivalence endpoint, and its simplicial lemma can also recover nonzero-degree selfmap rigidity over a suitable field. It does not cover arbitrary maps from higher-dimensional to lower-dimensional minimal sphere models. The older construction papers provide motivating examples rather than, in accessible material, a general obstruction.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The final claim is not a special case of the 2026 weak-equivalence theorem because its central assertion concerns all maps X_n to X_m with n>m, including nontrivial unstable homotopy groups. The new rank/collapse argument directly proves their nullity. Even if an inaccessible older paper contains a special low-dimensional obstruction, that would not by itself subsume the all-dimensions theorem; this remains a residual risk rather than a decisive unresolved comparison.

value.rationale: The claim gives a uniform map-level limitation of the smallest finite sphere models, not merely another space-minimality count. It explains why known finite-poset constructions of Hopf/Whitehead-type maps enlarge or subdivide their sphere models and identifies a sharp baseline for future questions about the minimum extra complexity needed to represent a prescribed nontrivial sphere map.
